subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram pairing approvals become a one-tap native callback path, and what sender binding, scope, expiry, and replay rules must that path enforce?
rationale: A Telegram button could approve DM/device pairing and sometimes operator-admin browser requests, so automation should not choose the trust model or broaden command-owner scopes without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design guarded pairing callbacks first
options.body: Define a typed device-pair callback contract that preserves current scope checks, request binding, expiry, idempotency, and denial behavior before implementing Telegram buttons.

options.title: Limit to low-scope DM pairing only
options.body: Ship buttons only for pairing requests that need `operator.pairing`, while leaving admin/browser scope upgrades on the existing CLI or Control UI path.

options.title: Fold into broader approval cards
options.body: Pause this issue until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92666 defines the shared channel-aware device approval card contract.

recommendation.title: Design guarded pairing callbacks first
recommendation.body: Define a typed device-pair callback contract that preserves current scope checks, request binding, expiry, idempotency, and denial behavior before implementing Telegram buttons.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent history place Peter closest to the device-pair notification, auth, and Telegram callback surfaces involved in this decision.
